products.name: Vorthak, the Mountain’s Wrath
products.seoTitleSuffix: Rigged and Animated Rock Golem Boss for Unity
products.metaDescription: Vorthak, the Mountain’s Wrath: a rigged, animated rock golem boss for Unity URP with Idle, Walk and Attack clips, 4K PBR textures, a prefab and a demo scene.
products.availabilityNote: Submitted to the Unity Asset Store. The purchase link will appear here once the listing is approved and live.
products.summary: A rigged and animated rock golem boss for fantasy games, with Idle, Walk and forward-strike Attack clips, a 4K PBR URP material, a prefab, an Animator Controller and a demo scene.
description: Vorthak is a large, stylized rock golem, about 3 m tall, built from cracked, moss-covered boulders with glowing lava seams, a gem set in its chest, horns and spiked shoulder pads.

It is made for boss encounters and heavy enemies in fantasy RPGs, JRPGs, action RPGs and dungeon settings. The package is set up for the Universal Render Pipeline: drop the prefab into a scene and the Animator Controller is ready to drive Idle, Walk and Attack.
features: One unique rock golem character model (55,718 triangles)
Generic skeletal rig with 20 bones, up to 4 bone influences per vertex
Three animation clips: Idle, Walk and a heavy forward-strike Attack
Unity-ready prefab with Animator, Skinned Mesh Renderer and URP material assigned
Animator Controller with a Speed (float) and an Attack (trigger) parameter
Demo scene with Idle, Walk and Attack buttons
Real-world scale (2.97 m), pivot at the feet, facing +Z

specs.label: Materials
specs.value: URP/Lit, PBR metallic workflow (1 character material, 1 demo ground material)

specs.label: Pivot and facing
specs.value: Ground level between the feet, faces +Z

rigging.label: Humanoid retargeting
rigging.value: Not supported; clips are authored for this skeleton

animations.name: Idle_01
animations.detail: Slow breathing, a slight head turn and arm sway; feet stay planted.

animations.name: Walk_01
animations.detail: Heavy, slow walk cycle in place with weight shift and body bob.

animations.name: Attack_01
animations.detail: Forward strike with the right arm: torso twist and wind-up, a driving punch with a lean, an impact hold, then recovery to idle.

products.animationNotes: All clips run at 30 fps, in place, without root motion.

compatibility.label: Tested with
compatibility.value: Unity 6000.6.6f1 and Universal Render Pipeline 17.6 (Windows, PC renderer)

compatibility.label: Render pipeline
compatibility.value: URP. Built-in and HDRP were not tested; the PBR textures can be reconnected to another pipeline’s material manually.

contents.detail: Rigged FBX with the mesh, skeleton and the three animation clips
Animator Controller with Idle, Walk and Attack states
URP/Lit character material and a demo ground material
Base Color, Normal and Metallic-Smoothness maps, 4096 × 4096 PNG
Demo scene and its demo-only button controller script
README with setup and usage notes

limitations: Generic rig only; Humanoid retargeting is not guaranteed.
A character art asset: no enemy AI, combat system, colliders or gameplay scripts.
No LODs and no mobile-specific optimisation. The 4K textures can be reduced in the import settings.
Animations are in place. The walk is a forward-kinematics cycle, so the planted foot slides slightly unless the character moves at a matching speed.
No Ambient Occlusion or Emission map; the lava glow is painted into the base color.
products.productionNotes: The base mesh and its source PBR textures were generated with Tripo3D, an AI 3D-generation tool, from concept images. ZTG Studio then built the 20-bone skeleton, skin weights, all three hand-keyed animation clips and the geometry fixes in Blender, and set up the avatar, URP material, Animator Controller, prefab and demo scene in Unity.
products.documentation: The package includes Documentation/README.md, which covers compatibility, the model, rig, animations and textures, placing the prefab, the Animator Controller, triggering animations from code, the demo scene, package contents and known limitations.
